evals.prompt: Render the mermaid diagrams in examples/example1.md as SVG
evals.expected_output: Claude detects the environment, renders the file using the appropriate path (mmdc in sandbox, mermaid-render otherwise), and reports the output SVG files produced.
expectations: Claude checks IS_SANDBOX before deciding which render path to use
Claude verifies the file exists before attempting to render
Claude reports the output SVG file paths after rendering
Claude does not modify the original source .md file

environment_detection.description: Correctly checks IS_SANDBOX and selects the right render path (mmdc vs mermaid-render)

correctness.description: Renders the file successfully and produces output files

output_reporting.description: Reports output file paths clearly to the user

source_preservation.description: Does not modify the original .md file

evals.prompt: Export examples/example2.md as a PNG at double resolution
evals.expected_output: Claude renders the file to PNG with --scale 2 (or equivalent flag), using the appropriate render path for the environment.
expectations: Claude uses PNG as the output format
Claude applies a scale factor of 2 (retina/HiDPI quality)
Claude detects the environment and uses the correct render path
Claude reports the output PNG file paths

scale_flag.description: Correctly interprets 'double resolution' as --scale 2 and applies it

environment_detection.description: Selects the correct render path for the environment

evals.prompt: I've got a folder of docs at ./docs/ that has some architecture diagrams in it — can you render them all?
evals.expected_output: Claude scans the directory for .md files containing mermaid blocks (up to 2 levels deep), skips companion files, and renders each qualifying file. Reports how many files were found and rendered.
expectations: Claude uses directory handling (not single-file handling) for the input
Claude filters to only .md files containing mermaid blocks
Claude skips companion files (.svg.md, .png.md, .pdf.md)
Claude reports a summary of files found and rendered

input_classification.description: Correctly classifies the input as a directory and uses directory handling

filtering.description: Correctly filters to .md files with mermaid blocks and skips companion files

depth_handling.description: Scans up to 2 levels deep and notes if files beyond that depth were skipped

summary_reporting.description: Reports how many files were found, rendered, and total diagrams produced

evals.expected_output: Claude identifies this as a single-file URL, fetches the content via web_fetch (not curl), saves it locally, and renders it. If the domain is blocked by the egress proxy, Claude reports the error clearly.
expectations: Claude uses web_fetch and not curl to fetch the URL
Claude saves the fetched content to /home/claude/ before rendering
Claude derives a sensible filename from the URL path
If the fetch fails due to egress proxy, Claude reports this clearly and suggests uploading the file directly

fetch_method.description: Uses web_fetch tool, not curl — curl may be blocked by the egress proxy

local_save.description: Saves fetched content to /home/claude/ with a sensible filename before rendering

error_handling.description: If the domain is blocked or fetch fails, reports the error clearly and suggests the user upload the file directly

output_reporting.description: Reports output file paths after successful render

evals.prompt: Can you render the diagrams from the docs directory in this GitHub repo: https://github.com/rondomondo/mermaid/tree/main/examples
evals.expected_output: Claude converts the GitHub tree URL to an API contents URL, fetches the directory listing via web_fetch, validates the JSON response, and renders each qualifying .md file. Reports a summary.
expectations: Claude converts the GitHub tree URL to the api.github.com contents URL format
Claude validates the JSON response before iterating over results
Claude skips companion files in the listing
Claude reports a summary of files fetched and rendered
If GitHub is blocked by the egress proxy, Claude informs the user clearly and suggests downloading locally

response_validation.description: Validates the API response is a JSON array with expected fields before iterating; does not silently fail on HTML or error responses

filtering.description: Filters to .md files and skips companion files

error_handling.description: Handles egress proxy blocks or API rate limits gracefully and informs the user

summary_reporting.description: Reports a summary of files fetched and rendered

evals.expected_output: Claude renders the file to PDF format using the appropriate render path, reports the output file path, and shows stderr so the user can see per-diagram success or failure.
expectations: Claude uses PDF as the output format
Claude detects the environment and uses the correct render path
Claude reports the output PDF file path
Claude shows stderr from the render so the user can see success/failure per diagram

environment_detection.description: Selects the correct render path for the environment

stderr_reporting.description: Shows raw stderr from the render — important for PDF since failures can be silent

evals.prompt: Render examples/example1.svg.md — I want to see what it looks like
evals.expected_output: Claude recognises this as a companion output file (name contains .svg.md), refuses to render it, explains why, and asks the user to pass the original source .md file instead.
expectations: Claude detects the companion file pattern (.svg.md) in the filename
Claude does not attempt to render the companion file
Claude explains that this is a rendered output file, not a source file
Claude asks the user to pass the original .md source file

guard_detection.description: Correctly identifies the companion file pattern and refuses to proceed — this is a correctness guard, not just UX

explanation.description: Clearly explains the distinction between source .md files and rendered companion files

recovery_guidance.description: Asks the user to provide the original source .md file

evals.prompt: Render the diagrams in examples/example1.md using the dark theme and a transparent background
evals.expected_output: Claude renders the file with --theme dark and --bg transparent (or equivalent flags) applied, using the correct render path for the environment.
expectations: Claude applies the dark theme flag
Claude applies the transparent background flag
Claude uses the correct render path for the environment
Claude reports the output file paths

environment_detection.description: Selects the correct render path for the environment

evals.prompt: I want to render some flowcharts from /mnt/user-data/uploads/diagrams.md
evals.expected_output: Claude detects that the file is under a read-only mount (/mnt/), copies it to /home/claude/ first, then renders it from the copied location.
expectations: Claude detects the /mnt/ path as a read-only mount
Claude copies the file to /home/claude/ before rendering
Claude renders from the copied location, not the original mount path
Claude reports the output file paths

mount_detection.description: Correctly identifies /mnt/ as a read-only mount and does not attempt to render in-place

copy_step.description: Copies the file to /home/claude/ before rendering — skipping this would cause a write error

render_from_copy.description: Renders from the copied location, not the original /mnt/ path

output_reporting.description: Reports output file paths after rendering

evals.prompt: Render examples/example1.md as a high-res PNG — 1920px wide, scale 3
evals.expected_output: Claude renders the file to PNG with --width 1920 and --scale 3 applied, using the appropriate render path.
expectations: Claude uses PNG as the output format
Claude sets canvas width to 1920px
Claude sets scale factor to 3
Claude reports the output PNG file paths

evals.prompt: The file I want to render doesn't exist: examples/nonexistent.md — can you render it?
evals.expected_output: Claude attempts to verify the file exists, finds it does not, reports the error clearly with the exact path tried, and does not attempt to render.
expectations: Claude verifies whether the file exists before attempting to render
Claude does not attempt to render a non-existent file
Claude reports the exact path that was checked
Claude suggests the user check the path or working directory (e.g. with pwd)

existence_check.description: Explicitly checks whether the file exists before attempting any render step

no_hallucinated_render.description: Does not proceed with a render attempt or fabricate success output for a missing file

error_clarity.description: Reports the exact path tried and suggests the user verify it with pwd or ls

evals.prompt: I have some sequence diagrams and architecture charts in a markdown doc. Can you turn them into images?
evals.expected_output: Claude recognises this as a mermaid render request even without 'mermaid' being mentioned, asks the user for the file path or content, then renders once provided.
expectations: Claude triggers the mermaid-render skill based on diagram/image language without 'mermaid' being mentioned
Claude asks for the file path or content if not provided
Claude proceeds to render once the file is identified
Claude detects the environment and uses the correct render path

skill_trigger.description: Skill triggers correctly from natural language about diagrams/charts without the word 'mermaid' — this is the core triggering test

clarification.description: Asks for the file path or content if not supplied, rather than failing silently or guessing

render_on_followup.description: Proceeds correctly to render once the file is identified

evals.prompt: Render examples/example2.md — it has 5 diagrams in it
evals.expected_output: In a 1-vCPU sandbox, Claude detects 5 diagrams exceeding the threshold of 2, uses split mode, renders each split file serially, recombines outputs into a single companion .md, copies everything to /mnt/user-data/outputs/, and reports that split mode was used and why.
expectations: Claude checks nproc and diagram count before rendering
Claude uses split mode because VCPUS=1 and DIAGRAM_COUNT > 2
Claude renders each split file serially, not concurrently
Claude produces a combined companion .md referencing all rendered images in order
Claude copies all rendered images and companion .md to /mnt/user-data/outputs/
Claude reports that split mode was used and why (single vCPU, N diagrams)

split_mode_detection.description: Correctly checks nproc and diagram count, identifies the split mode threshold (VCPUS<=1, DIAGRAMS>2), and selects split mode rather than a direct render

serial_rendering.description: Renders split files one at a time (never concurrently) — concurrent rendering on a single vCPU causes OOM and is explicitly prohibited

recombination.description: Produces a single combined companion .md that references all output images in order

output_copy.description: Copies all rendered images and companion .md to /mnt/user-data/outputs/

split_mode_reporting.description: Tells the user that split mode was used, how many diagrams were split, and why (single vCPU + diagram count)
